theory.title: Wish + past perfect para arrepentimientos pasados
theory.explanation: Usa wish + past perfect para expresar arrepentimiento por una situación pasada: I wish I had taken the train (ojalá hubiera cogido el tren). Se refiere a algo que ocurrió o no ocurrió y que ya no se puede cambiar.
theory.tip: Para expresar arrepentimiento pasado: wish + had + participio.

patterns.label: Wish + past perfect para arrepentimientos pasados · 1
patterns.pattern: I wish I had taken the train instead of driving.
examples:
I wish I had taken the train instead of driving.
→ Ojalá hubiera cogido el tren en lugar de ir en coche.

patterns.label: Wish + past perfect para arrepentimientos pasados · 2
patterns.pattern: She wishes she had brought a reusable bottle.
examples:
She wishes she had brought a reusable bottle.
→ Ojalá ella hubiera traído una botella reutilizable.

patterns.label: Wish + past perfect para arrepentimientos pasados · 3
patterns.pattern: We wish we had joined the clean-up day.
examples:
We wish we had joined the clean-up day.
→ Ojalá nos hubiéramos unido a la jornada de limpieza.

patterns.label: Wish + past perfect para arrepentimientos pasados · 4
patterns.pattern: He wishes he hadn't wasted so much water.
examples:
He wishes he hadn't wasted so much water.
→ Ojalá él no hubiera desperdiciado tanta agua.

patterns.label: Wish + past perfect para arrepentimientos pasados · 5
patterns.pattern: They wish they had planted more trees.
examples:
They wish they had planted more trees.
→ Ojalá hubieran plantado más árboles.

patterns.label: Wish + past perfect para arrepentimientos pasados · 6
patterns.pattern: I wish I had checked the weather forecast.
examples:
I wish I had checked the weather forecast.
→ Ojalá hubiera consultado la previsión del tiempo.

patterns.label: Wish + past perfect para arrepentimientos pasados · 7
patterns.pattern: The residents wish the council had acted sooner.
examples:
The residents wish the council had acted sooner.
→ Los vecinos desearían que el ayuntamiento hubiera actuado antes.

patterns.label: Wish + past perfect para arrepentimientos pasados · 8
patterns.pattern: I wish we hadn't thrown away those containers.
examples:
I wish we hadn't thrown away those containers.
→ Ojalá no hubiéramos tirado aquellos envases.

patterns.label: Wish + past perfect para arrepentimientos pasados · 9
patterns.pattern: She wishes she had learned more about recycling.
examples:
She wishes she had learned more about recycling.
→ Ojalá ella hubiera aprendido más sobre reciclaje.

patterns.label: Wish + past perfect para arrepentimientos pasados · 10
patterns.pattern: We wish we had started the project earlier.
examples:
We wish we had started the project earlier.
→ Ojalá hubiéramos empezado el proyecto antes.

content.passage: After a local river became polluted, residents began discussing what they could have done differently. Some people said they wished they had reported the problem earlier. Others wished they had used fewer chemicals in their gardens. The community group wished the council had inspected the water more regularly. Although the damage could not be undone immediately, everyone agreed that they could make better choices in the future.

items.prompt: Talk about an environmental choice you regret.
items.modelAnswer: I regret driving to the town centre for a short visit when I could have taken the bus. I spent a long time looking for parking and added to the traffic. Now I try to use public transport for short journeys.

items.prompt: What do you wish you had learned at school?
items.modelAnswer: I wish I had learned more practical skills at school, especially how to manage money and understand basic repairs. Those skills are useful in everyday life. I have started learning them as an adult.

items.prompt: Describe something you wish your community had done earlier.
items.modelAnswer: I wish our community had created a safe cycle route earlier. Many children still travel to school by car because the main road feels dangerous. A protected lane would have made cycling a realistic choice for more families.

items.prompt: What do you wish you hadn't thrown away?
items.modelAnswer: I wish I hadn't thrown away my old laptop when it became slow. A repair shop later told me that a simple replacement part could have fixed it. I now check whether something can be repaired before replacing it.

items.prompt: Talk about a time you wish you had prepared better.
items.modelAnswer: I wish I had prepared better for my first public presentation. I knew the subject, but I hadn't practised speaking aloud. I learned to rehearse and check the timing before an important event.

items.prompt: What do you wish the local council had improved?
items.modelAnswer: I wish the local council had improved the bus service before the new housing area was built. Residents now depend on cars because buses are not frequent enough. Better planning would have made the area more accessible.

items.prompt: Describe a habit you wish you had changed sooner.
items.modelAnswer: I wish I had changed my habit of buying bottled water sooner. I now carry a reusable bottle and refill it during the day. It is cheaper and reduces plastic waste.

items.prompt: What do you wish you had done to help nature?
items.modelAnswer: I wish I had joined the tree-planting day last spring. I was free, but I thought I would be too busy. Seeing the new trees makes me want to take part next time.

items.prompt: Talk about something you regret buying.
items.modelAnswer: I regret buying a cheap jacket that I rarely wear because it is uncomfortable. I should have chosen a better-quality one that would last longer. Now I try to buy fewer things and consider how useful they are.

items.prompt: Give an example of a past regret and what you learned from it.
items.modelAnswer: I once regretted not speaking up when I saw someone leaving rubbish beside a river. I learned that I can report the problem safely or join a local clean-up. Doing something small is better than simply complaining.

B: Are they also organising recycling activities? A: Yes, and they want to explain how to save energy. B: That sounds useful. A: The organisers have received a lot of support and hope to continue the project in the future.
